script.base: As-of pack only: Pittsburgh is a 3-point road favorite in a 43 total (implied about 23-20), so the base flow is a close game with PIT ahead late, not a shootout. PIT leans on Jaylen Warren (46 carries, 244 yards over weeks 4-6) into a Saints run defense allowing 5.07 YPC, while Aaron Rodgers (EPA/dropback -0.34 vs blitz, n=76, vs -0.05 unblitzed) checks down when New Orleans brings a 34% blitz. New Orleans stays competitive through Chris Olave (25 targets, 205 yards, 310 air yards L3); Kendre Miller's 36 carries produced only 109 yards (3.03 YPC) and does not take the game over.
script.flip1: PIT jumps ahead and clocks it. Warren's carries hold or rise and DK Metcalf's deep shots (288 air yards on 28 targets L3) stall; Miller's rush work dies because the dog abandons the run. Warren rush+rec still has a path; Olave/Metcalf overs do not.
script.flip2: The Saints' 34% blitz actually buries Rodgers (-0.34 EPA vs blitz), PIT falls behind and abandons the run, and Warren's 15-carry pace breaks. His checkdown role (17 targets, 148 yards, -15 air yards L3) can save a combined number but a rush-only over would not. The other miss is a shootout: both defenses have allowed explosives (NO 20 of 213, PIT 21 of 217) and the 43 total is too low, which helps Olave/Metcalf and hurts quiet skill unders.

matchup.pressure: Saints blitz rate 34%; Steelers blitz rate 26%. Pressure rate is not in the pack. Rodgers is -0.34 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=76) vs -0.05 with no blitz, so a blitz-heavy Saints plan threatens deep shots and pushes quick throws. Shough is -0.17 vs blitz (n=93) and +0.07 unblitzed, and PIT's 26% blitz rate leaves him more clean dropbacks.
matchup.bleeds: Saints bleed the run (5.07 YPC, 21 runs of 10+) and the middle/left pass. Steelers are the better run front (4.19 YPC, 17 runs of 10+) with no pass location above 6.88 YPA. Explosive passes are similar (NO 20/213 att, PIT 21/217).
matchup.overlap: The overlap that survives the blitz profile is Warren: 15.3 carries/game at 5.30 YPC into a 5.07 YPC defense, plus a negative-air-yard receiving role (17 targets, -15 air yards) that a 34% blitz and a -0.34 blitz-EPA quarterback feed. Metcalf's 288 air yards would attack the soft left/middle, but that is the shot the blitz profile threatens, so it is not the leg. Olave's 310 air yards do not map to a Steelers location hole.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Warren is the bellcow (46 carries, 244 yards in three games, 5.30 YPC) running into a defense allowing 5.07 YPC, and New Orleans' 34% blitz plus Rodgers' -0.34 blitz EPA add the checkdowns that already produced 148 receiving yards, so 96.5 rush+rec is light if he keeps a full role.
edge_players.must_be_true: Warren plays his recent snap/carry share (about 14+ carries, not a Dowdle takeover), is not a late inactive or snap-limited, and the game stays close or PIT-led so the run lean holds; a trailing script still needs the checkdown piece.
edge_players.kills_it: Receiving YAC craters off the -15 air-yard profile and carries fall under 12 because PIT trails and abandons the run, or Warren is limited and Dowdle (only 7 carries L3, but the rush over 28.5 is the juiced side at -117.5) takes the work.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Kamara just posted about 44 rush+rec yards a game (69 rush + 64 receiving on 17 carries and 13 targets) against a 32.5 line, and the PIT-control script that hurts his carries pushes him into the dump-off role that already cleared the number without needing a Miller-sized rushing day.
edge_players.must_be_true: Kamara is active in his L3 passing-down role (about 4 targets, not a healthy scratch) and Miller does not turn this into a 20-carry grind that leaves Kamara off the field.
edge_players.kills_it: New Orleans leads and clocks it with Miller (36 carries L3 vs Kamara's 17) while Shough, who is better unblitzed (+0.07 EPA) against a 26% PIT blitz, throws to Olave and Vele instead of the checkdown, leaving Kamara around 15 rush plus 10 receiving.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Warren over 96.5 lost because the 148 receiving yards on -15 air yards were a screen spike that came back as 10 yards, Pittsburgh fell behind under the Saints' 34% blitz, Rodgers' -0.34 blitz EPA forced a dropback script, and Warren finished something like 11 carries for 48 with Dowdle mixing in — 96.5 needed both the carry stack and the YAC, and only a piece of one showed up. Kamara over 32.5 lost on the same card if New Orleans somehow controlled the clock anyway: Miller took 18 carries, Kamara saw 2 carries and 1 target, and Shough's clean-pocket EPA went to Olave (310 air yards L3) rather than a 13-air-yard dump-off. The Warren counter is real but not stronger than a 5.30 YPC bellcow into a 5.07 YPC front as a 3-point favorite; the Kamara counter is close enough that the leg stays a lean, not a strong.
slip_story: One script: Pittsburgh's favorite-side run/checkdown game against a soft Saints front and a 34% blitz, total staying near 43 rather than a shootout. Warren rush+rec over is the anchor and wins with the base case and with the PIT-leads flip; Kamara rush+rec over belongs only as the correlated dog-throws piece of that same PIT-control story, not as a NO-grind leg. Do not add Metcalf or Olave overs (they need the dropback/explosive flip), do not add a game under next to pass-catcher overs, no TD legs, and no second market on either player.
